newsitem.title: UK: Unilever shares hit record high.
newsitem.headline: Unilever shares hit record high.

text.p: Unilever NV shares touched an all-time best on Wednesday, boosted by positive feedback from analysts meetings in New York and by its plans for expanding in emerging markets, traders said.
A stronger food manufacturing sector also lifted Unilever's stock to a record 18.72 stg. By 1400 GMT, the shares were up 27-1/2p at 18.65 stg.
"There is a bit of talk about emerging market...there is feedback (on the analysts meeting) and the food manufacturers are stronger today," one trader said.
Unilever said executives are briefing analysts at an event sponsored by Goldman Sachs.
In an interview with Reuters, Chairman Niall Fitzgerald said the Anglo-Dutch consumer group was set on expansion in the developing and emerging markets of the Far East and Latin America.

"There will certainly be a larger proportion of the business in developing and emerging markets in five years time," said Fitzgerald, who set a target of 50 percent of trading profits from these markets in seven years time compared with its current 30 percent.
Since raising $8 billion from the sale of its four speciality businesses to ICI Plc in July, the market has been rife with speculation Unilever will mount a take-over.
The take-over talk has driven shares in Reckitt and Coleman, Cadbury-Schweppes Plc and Groupe Danon, among others.
In other share activity, Cadbury-Schweppes stock jumped 14-1/2p to 610p, after half-year results were reported within expectations and the company reassured over its leading soft drink brands.
The company said it made pre-tax profit of 236 million stg against 231 million stg last time and compared with forecasts of 227-246 million.
